document_metadata.title: 8、INT. KRAMER'S OFFICE -- DAY
document_metadata.summary: Ross interviews Daniels in Turin, showing evidence linking Bourne to past events and Marie's death, while questioning Treadstone's role; Daniels demands the recorder be turned off.

chunks.content: Kramer listens to a recording with Landy and Cronin. There are unhung pictures and a few other items that indicate he has just moved into this job. Two other senior CIA officials sit in on the meeting. Kramer looks at a file on Bourne and Abbott. BOURNE (V.O.) So we got in the way? Is that why Neski died? Is that why you killed Marie? Kramer glances at a photo of Marie in the file. ABBOTT (V.O.) You killed Marie the minute you climbed into her car. The minute you entered her life she was dead! Kramer looks at Abbott's official photo. BOURNE (V.O.) I told you people to leave me alone! I fell off the grid. I was half way around the world. ABBOTT (V.O.) There's no place it won't catch up to you. It's how every story ends. It's what you are, Jason. A killer! You always will be. THUMP! CRONIN We think that's Bourne hitting him on the head and then-- He makes a gun with his hand, i.e. Bourne putting his gun to Abbott's head. ABBOTT (V.O.) Go ahead! Go on! Do it! BOURNE (V.O.) She wouldn't want me to. That's the only reason your alive. The tape clicks off. KRAMER Who's \"she?\" CRONIN puts a picture of MARIE in front of KRAMER. LANDY His girlfriend, Marie. She was killed in India three weeks ago. Kramer looks down at another image. Abbott dead after his suicide. KRAMER A dirty section chief in league with a corrupt Russian Billionaire commits suicide when confronted by Jason Bourne. You couldn't make this stuff up. (holds up the photo of Abbot dead) You watched this happen? Landy nods. Kramer shakes his head in disgust at the whole situation. KRAMER Bourne's last confirmed location is Moscow, three days ago? LANDY Right. KRAMER So what does he do now? LANDY I think he's looking for something he hasn't found. KRAMER Like what? What's he after? LANDY I'm not sure. Maybe he hasn't gotten his memory back yet. Not all of it. A look from Kramer... KRAMER Pam, what I need to know is, what kind of a threat is he to us? LANDY If he just wanted to hurt us he could have sent this tape to CNN. KRAMER Maybe he still will. Maybe he gave it to you because he wants to throw you in the opposite direction of his real plan. I don't know. I just know my number one rule is \"the only way to stay safe is to assume the worst.\" As far as I'm concerned Bourne is a serious threat until proven otherwise.

chunks.content: The charm of old Paris captured in the workings of an elevator operating in a wrought-iron shaft... A WORK TABLE, covered with sheet music, music paper, pencils. document_metadata.title: 90、EXT. PLATFORM AREA -- DAY
document_metadata.summary: Bourne sees Paz on a train, recognizes a reflection of his past self, and resumes the chase as the train departs.

chunks.content: BOURNE is tailing PAZ down onto a parallel platform as PAZ dips into the underground entrance. Inside the Waterloo Tube Station during the evening rush hour, PAZ moves deliberately, blending seamlessly into the crowd. BOURNE follows close behind, driven by instinct rather than strategy. He catches a fleeting glimpse of PAZ at the bottom of an escalator and pushes through the throng of commuters, urgency mounting. Despite his efforts, PAZ vanishes into the dense flow of people, forcing BOURNE to sprint ahead, rounding a corner to find a long walkway ending in two staircases leading to separate tube lines. BOURNE hesitates momentarily, weighing his options as the sound of an approaching train echoes through the station.

metadata.title: 90、EXT. PLATFORM AREA -- DAY
metadata.summary: Bourne sees Paz on a train, recognizes a reflection of his past self, and resumes the chase as the train departs.

chunks.content: He makes his decision and rushes downstairs, just in time to see PAZ stepping into a train car through another door. BOURNE lunges forward, but the doors close before he can board. From the platform, he watches as PAZ slumps into a seat, visibly unwell—his skin clammy, head pounding, clearly suffering. PAZ pulls out a bottle of pills and dry-swallows several, then lifts his gaze. The moment is striking: BOURNE stares at PAZ as if looking into a mirror, seeing his former self—the man he was before he became Jason Bourne, before identity was stripped away and rebuilt through violence and survival. There’s a haunting familiarity in PAZ’s weariness, a reflection of a life lived in shadows.CLOSE ON PAZ—he looks straight ahead, indistinguishable from any other commuter, anonymous in the rhythm of the city. BACK ON BOURNE, still on the platform, watching as the train pulls away, carrying PAZ into the tunnels. The connection lingers in his eyes, a silent recognition. Then, without hesitation, BOURNE is immediately in motion again, resuming the chase, the pursuit reignited.

In the present, Hirsch reflects on Bourne’s past as a soldier eager to serve, unlike others not only for his patriotism but for his exceptional skills in languages and marksmanship. Another flashback surfaces: Hirsch telling the younger Bourne that his missions will save American lives. Bourne, now in the present, counters bitterly that instead of saving lives, he was turned into a killer. He raises his gun at Hirsch, who insists Bourne could have left at any time and knew the consequences of staying. A further flashback returns to the moment of transformation: Hirsch confronting a sleep-deprived Bourne, demanding a decision—whether to let go of David Webb and fully commit to the program.

Pressured, Bourne looks down at a gun in his hand. He rises suddenly and fires multiple shots into the hooded figure, who collapses. Stunned, Bourne stares at the body. Hirsch declares the act final: David Webb is gone. From now on, he is Jason Bourne—welcome to the program. Daniels removes the hood, revealing the man is dead. At that moment, Kramer enters and confirms Bourne is ready, ordering him sent to Operations. The memory fades as Bourne returns to the present, eyes locked on Hirsch. Hirsch asks if he remembers now. Bourne lowers the gun and affirms he remembers everything—the truth of his transformation. Hirsch insists Bourne can’t escape what he chose; he made himself into Jason Bourne.Bourne declares he’s done running—that’s why he’s here: to end Hirsch and shut down the program. He asserts he is no longer Jason Bourne. Hirsch challenges him, asking if he’s going to kill him now. Bourne refuses, stating Hirsch doesn’t deserve the honor of a star on the wall at Langley. In that moment, Bourne spins around as agents arrive at the door—it’s locked.
